failures.title: Peugeot EB2ADTS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Wet Belt Degradation - The PureTech's Most Notorious Issue
items.onset: 40,000-80,000 miles (dependent on oil quality and change intervals)
items.whatHappens: The EB2ADTS uses a wet timing belt that runs in the engine oil. Over time, the belt degrades and sheds material into the oil system. This debris blocks the oil pickup strainer, leading to oil starvation, low oil pressure, and ultimately catastrophic engine failure. This is the single biggest failure point on the PureTech engine and has been the subject of multiple recalls and technical campaigns. The issue is particularly prevalent on engines with long oil change intervals or incorrect oil specification.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early (before oil pressure drops), belt replacement is a specialist job (£600-£1,200) and includes cleaning the oil pickup strainer. If the engine has suffered oil starvation due to a blocked pickup, the bottom end (crankshaft bearings, conrod bearings) is usually damaged - in this case, a full replacement is the only safe option. Read our full wet belt failure guide

items.title: Fuel Injector Failure - Misfires & Rough Running
items.whatHappens: The EB2ADTS uses direct injection, and the injectors can become clogged or fail electrically. Symptoms include misfires, rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, and check-engine lights. This is particularly common on cars that have been used primarily for short urban journeys.
items.repairVsReplace: Injector cleaning or replacement is a straightforward job (£300-£600 per injector). Replacement of all three injectors is often recommended as a preventative measure if one has failed, as the others are likely to follow soon. Read our full fuel system failure guide

items.title: Ignition Coil Failure - Misfires & Reduced Power
items.whatHappens: The EB2ADTS's ignition coils can fail, causing misfires and reduced power. This is more common on older examples (2012-2018) and can be triggered by heat and vibration.
items.repairVsReplace: Coil replacement is straightforward (£150-£300 per coil). Replacement of all three coils is often recommended as a preventative measure.

failures.goodYearsLine: The EB2ADTS was revised from 2018 onwards with improved belt materials and revised service schedules. Post-2018 engines are significantly more reliable, but the wet belt remains a scheduled maintenance item with a recommended replacement interval of 6 years or 60,000 miles (reduced from the original 10-year/100,000-mile schedule). Always use the correct oil specification (PSA B71 2300/2312) - using the wrong oil accelerates belt degradation.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the EB2ADTS
variants.intro: The EB2ADTS is the 110 hp version of Peugeot's 1.2 PureTech engine. It's part of the EB2 family, which includes naturally aspirated versions and higher-output turbocharged variants. The EB2ADTS is distinguished by its 110 hp output, specific turbocharger calibration, and emissions compliance. Where the code appears: - Stamped on a metal plate on the engine block (left-hand side, near the timing cover) - On the V5C logbook under "Engine number" (the first 7 characters will read EB2ADTS) - Via VIN decoder - the PureTech engine family is identified by the model designation Commonly confused with: - EB2DTS - 130 hp higher-output version, different turbocharger and ECU calibration - EB2 - 1.2L naturally aspirated (82 hp), no turbocharger - EB2ADT - 1.2L turbo with 110 hp, earlier version before ADTS designation

relatives.description: - the 1.6‑litre turbocharged four‑cylinder that preceded the EB2 family in many Peugeot and Citroën models. Known for timing chain stretch and high‑pressure fuel pump failure - the EB2 family was designed to be simpler and more efficient, but introduced its own wet belt issues.

EB2ADTS (updated versions) / - the 130 hp higher‑output version of the 1.2 PureTech. Shares the same block but has different turbocharger and ECU calibration. Also, from 2023 onwards, Stellantis has been transitioning to the third‑generation EB2 with revised belt materials and improved oil pump design.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EB2ADTS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used EB2ADTS can make sense for lower-value Peugeot 208 or Citroën C3 models where the car's value doesn't justify a recon unit. However, the wet belt is the single biggest risk - only consider a used unit with documented proof of recent belt replacement (within the last 30,000 miles or 3 years). Without that, factor in £600-£1,200 for belt replacement and oil system cleaning. Link once: /services/used-engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper EB2ADTS recon is the best option for owners planning to keep their car long-term. A quality recon should include: full strip and inspection, new wet belt and tensioner (critical), new injectors, new ignition coils, new gaskets and seals, and a full oil system flush. With a 12-24 month warranty, this gives you peace of mind that the engine's known weaknesses have been addressed - well worth the £1,200-£2,200 supply cost. Link once: /services/reconditioned-engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified when the original engine has suffered catastrophic failure (oil starvation due to blocked pickup, seized bottom end) and the car is a cherished keeper or low-mileage example. An upgraded rebuild should include new crankshaft bearings, conrod bearings, new pistons/rings if damaged, refreshed cylinder head, and a full oil system flush. This is specialist territory and typically only makes sense for cars with strong residual value. Link once: /services/rebuilt-engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted Peugeot specialists nationwide, with 12-month warranty on reconditioned and rebuilt units. Link once: /services/supply-and-fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The EB2ADTS sits in Peugeot 208, 308, 2008, Citroën C3, C4 and other Stellantis models - cars now worth £3,000-£18,000 depending on age and condition. With a reconditioned supply cost of £1,200-£2,200, replacement is viable on most examples. However, for a sub-£3,000 208 or C3 with high mileage and a failed engine, a used unit (£600-£1,200) with documented belt history may be the only sensible option. For cars worth under £2,000, consider breaking the car before committing to a replacement engine.

items.question: What is the wet belt problem on the EB2ADTS PureTech engine?
items.answer: The EB2ADTS uses a wet timing belt that runs in the engine oil. Over time, the belt degrades and sheds material into the oil system, blocking the oil pickup strainer. This leads to oil starvation, low oil pressure, and ultimately catastrophic engine failure. This is the single biggest failure point on the PureTech engine and has been subject to multiple recalls. Early symptoms: oil pressure warning light, rattling on start-up. Prevention: belt replacement at 6 years / 60,000 miles (revised schedule). Always use PSA B71 2300/2312 oil - incorrect oil accelerates belt degradation.

items.question: Which models use the EB2ADTS 1.2 PureTech engine?
items.answer: The EB2ADTS is fitted to Peugeot 208 (I & II), 308 (I & II), 2008 (I & II), 3008 (I), 5008 (I), Citroën C3 (III), C4 (II & III), C4 Cactus, DS 3, DS 4, and Opel/Vauxhall Corsa F and Mokka B. It's the 110 hp version of the 1.2 PureTech, sitting between the entry-level EB2 and the higher-output EB2DTS. Not to be confused with the EB2DTS (130 hp) or EB2 (82 hp naturally aspirated). The EB2ADTS is the most widely-fitted 1.2 PureTech variant in the UK.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned EB2ADTS engine?
items.answer: A used EB2ADTS can be viable for lower-value Peugeot 208 or Citroën C3 models, but only if it has documented proof of recent wet belt replacement (within the last 30,000 miles or 3 years). Without that, factor in £600-£1,200 for belt replacement and oil system cleaning. A reconditioned engine is the safer choice - it includes new wet belt, injectors, coils and gaskets, with a 12-24 month warranty. Used is cheaper (£600-£1,200) but wet belt risk is significant. Reconditioned addresses all known weak points and gives peace of mind.

items.question: How do I confirm if my car has the EB2ADTS or the EB2DTS?
items.answer: Check the engine code stamped on the block (left-hand side near the timing cover) - it will read EB2ADTS for the 110 hp variant, or EB2DTS for the 130 hp variant. The V5C logbook also lists the full engine number, with the first 7 characters identifying the code. EB2ADTS: 110 hp, specific turbocharger and ECU calibration. EB2DTS: 130 hp, larger turbocharger, different ECU and injectors. Fitting the wrong variant requires ECU reflash and potentially turbocharger changes - not a straight swap.
bullets: EB2ADTS: 110 hp, specific turbocharger and ECU calibration.
EB2DTS: 130 hp, larger turbocharger, different ECU and injectors.
Fitting the wrong variant requires ECU reflash and potentially turbocharger changes - not a straight swap.

items.question: How long does an EB2ADTS engine typically last?
items.answer: With meticulous maintenance and early preventative work, these engines can exceed 100,000-120,000 miles. The EB2ADTS is fundamentally a good engine; the limiting factor is the wet belt and the oil system. Wet belt replacement strongly recommended at 6 years / 60,000 miles. Regular oil changes (5,000-8,000 miles) with PSA B71 2300/2312 oil are essential. Never use non-approved oil - it accelerates belt degradation.
